definitions.explanation: a political party that opposes the ruling party or government

examples.japanese: {反対党|はんたいとう}が{法案|ほうあん}に{反対|はんたい}した。
examples.english: The opposition party opposed the bill.

examples.japanese: {反対党|はんたいとう}の{党首|とうしゅ}が{記者|きしゃ}{会見|かいけん}を{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: The leader of the opposition party held a press conference.

examples.japanese: {反対党|はんたいとう}は{政府|せいふ}の{経済|けいざい}{政策|せいさく}を{厳|きび}しく{批判|ひはん}し、{代替案|だいたいあん}を{提示|ていじ}した。
examples.english: The opposition party harshly criticized the government's economic policy and presented an alternative plan.

notes:
Composed of {反対|はんたい} (opposition) and {党|とう} (party). Refers to any political party opposing the ruling party or coalition. In Japanese politics, the main opposition has shifted over the decades, but the term itself is neutral and applies generically.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {反対党|はんたいとう}の{党首|とうしゅ}: opposition party leader
- {反対党|はんたいとう}が{批判|ひはん}する: the opposition criticizes
- {反対党|はんたいとう}の{主張|しゅちょう}: the opposition's claims
- {反対党|はんたいとう}に{転|てん}じる: to become an opposition party

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {野党|やとう}: opposition party — the standard, more common term in political discourse
- {与党|よとう}: ruling party — the party or coalition in power
- {対立|たいりつ}{政党|せいとう}: rival party — emphasizes the confrontational relationship
